change_summary: The alert records a retraction for this paper with no notice. The current copy's title is now marked 'RETRACTED:', while the stored paper's title was not. No notice text or reason for the retraction was available. The retraction affects the whole paper, including its headline finding that winter cover crops raised topsoil carbon by 6% over three years.
evaluation: Your draft cites Haugen and Rao [5] in Section 2.2 (Methods), saying you followed their protocol exactly for coring at 0-15 cm and dry-combustion carbon measurement. The paper's current copy is marked retracted and the alert records a retraction at high severity, and the retraction covers the whole paper including its sampling protocol. So the protocol you adopt in Section 2.2 is touched by the retraction. No notice or reason was available, so why it was retracted is unknown. The impact on you is high, because your methods rest directly on a retracted paper.
recommendation: The retraction is recorded only as a flag, with no notice or reason available. Your Methods section 2.2 says you followed the protocol of Haugen and Rao [5] exactly, so that use is touched by the retraction. First, check the journal's or publisher's page for the paper to confirm the retraction and find the reason. If confirmed, stop and raise it with your co-authors or supervisor, because your own sampling and measurement methods depend on this paper and editing the text won't fix that.
